newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Monday sold at prices steady to $1.00 per cwt lower than Friday's, pressured by lower pork prices, cash hog dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $46.00 to $47.00 in the country and $47.00 to $48.00, with a few at $48.50 at plants, sources there said.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $46.50 to $47.50 in the country and up to $48.00 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold steady at $46.00 to $47.00 in the country and $47.00 to $48.50 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady, at $46.00-$47.00 in the country and $48.00-$49.00 at plants.
Prices fell on lower pork prices late last week and projections for further price drops on Monday, sources said.
Pork cut-out values on Friday were quoted down $0.25 to $0.28 per cwt, USDA said.
"A combination of increased slaughter and sluggish pork demand pushed pork prices lower and could continue to do the same this week," said Dale Benson, market analyst with Dean-Witter Reynolds.
